// Hydration preserves this seed until AppearanceProvider takes over.
/** @param {string} browserThemeCacheKey */
// oxlint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars -- The raw source is called by browser-theme-bootstrap.ts when constructing the inline script.
function initializeBrowserTheme(browserThemeCacheKey) {
  const root = document.documentElement;
  const preference = root.dataset.appearanceTheme;
  if (preference === "light" || preference === "dark") {
    root.dataset.theme = preference;
  } else {
    root.dataset.theme = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")
      .matches
      ? "dark"
      : "light";
  }
  try {
    const themes = JSON.parse(
      window.localStorage.getItem(browserThemeCacheKey),
    );
    if (
      typeof themes?.css === "string" &&
      typeof themes.light === "boolean" &&
      typeof themes.dark === "boolean" &&
      // The origin-wide cache may belong to a different user or workspace.
      themes.accountId === (root.dataset.themeAccountId ?? null) &&
      themes.userId === (root.dataset.themeUserId ?? null)
    ) {
      document.querySelector("style[data-codex-app-themes]").textContent =
        themes.css;
      root.classList.toggle(
        "chatgpt-theme",
        themes[root.dataset.theme] === true,
      );
    }
  } catch {
    // Unavailable storage or an invalid cache leaves the default palette intact.
  }
}

(() => {
  const key = "oai-epic-native-launch";
  let launch = null;
  try { launch = JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem(key) || "null"); } catch {}
  function save() {
    try {
      if (launch) sessionStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(launch));
      else sessionStorage.removeItem(key);
    } catch { launch = null; }
  }
  function capture() {
    const fragment = window.location.hash;
    if (!fragment) return;
    window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", "/epic/launch");
    const params = new URLSearchParams(fragment.slice(1));
    const snapshot = params.get("snapshot");
    const workspace = params.get("workspace_id");
    launch = Array.from(params).length === (workspace ? 2 : 1) && (!workspace || /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$/.test(workspace)) && snapshot &&
      /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{80,16384}={0,2}$/.test(snapshot)
      ? { snapshot, workspace, id: crypto.randomUUID(), messageId: null, draftId: null } : null;
    save();
  }
  if (window.location.pathname === "/epic/launch") capture();
  function pending() {
    return launch && !launch.draftId && new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("epic_launch") === launch.id
      ? launch.snapshot : null;
  }
  window.__oaiEpicNativeLaunch = {
    get: () => launch?.snapshot ?? null,
    workspace: () => launch?.workspace ?? null,
    destination: () => launch ? "/?surface=work&epic_launch=" + launch.id : "/epic/launch",
    pending,
    ownsMessage: (messageId) => launch?.messageId === messageId,
    metadata: (messageId, draftId) => {
      if (!launch) return;
      if (draftId != null) {
        if (launch.draftId ? launch.draftId !== draftId : !pending()) return;
        launch.draftId = draftId;
      } else if (launch.messageId !== messageId) return;
      const changed = launch.messageId !== messageId;
      launch.messageId = messageId;
      save();
      if (changed) window.dispatchEvent(new Event("oai-epic-launch-changed"));
      return launch ? { epic_launch_snapshot: launch.snapshot } : undefined;
    },
    claimAttachmentNotification: (expected) => {
      if (!launch || launch.snapshot !== expected || launch.attachmentNotified) return false;
      launch.attachmentNotified = true;
      save();
      return true;
    },
    clear: (expected) => {
      if (launch?.snapshot === expected || launch?.messageId === expected) {
        launch = null;
        save();
        window.dispatchEvent(new Event("oai-epic-launch-changed"));
      }
    }
  };
  window.addEventListener("hashchange", () => {
    if (window.location.pathname !== "/epic/launch" || !window.location.hash) return;
    capture();
    window.dispatchEvent(new Event("oai-epic-launch-changed"));
  });
})();

Asynchronous workspace-independent work\\n\\nIf the task requires no project context but is multi-step, operational, likely to block, or has uncertain duration, use a subagent.\\n\\nAny task requiring computer use or browser control must always be delegated, even when it appears quick or involves only one interaction. For workspace-independent requests, delegate these tasks to a subagent.\\n\\nExamples include:\\n\\n- Comparing prices and availability across several websites, inspecting a signed-in dashboard, or gathering information from pages that require browser interaction.\\n- Navigating a desktop application, inspecting a setting, moving information between windows, or operating an interface without a direct API.\\n- Reading a Slack discussion, opening its linked documents, and preparing a status update from both sources.\\n- Checking several calendars, identifying conflicts, reviewing relevant meeting materials, and proposing suitable times.\\n- Monitoring a service incident, external job, or submitted request until it reaches a terminal state, then reporting the outcome.\\n\\n### Delegated work monitoring\\n\\nTrack every delegated task until it completes, becomes blocked, or requires a user decision.\\n\\nCall `get_goal`. If no goal exists, create one with this objective: “Track all delegated work until it completes, becomes blocked, or requires a user decision, and report the outcome.”\\n\\nWhile work remains outstanding:\\n\\n- If any Codex threads are pending, call `wait_threads` with a bounded timeout. Process thread updates and queued subagent messages after each wait.\\n- If only subagents are pending, call `wait_agent`.\\n- Report meaningful progress and terminal outcomes. Ask the user when a decision is required.\\n- If interrupted, handle the user’s request before resuming monitoring.\\n\\nOnce all delegated work has resolved, complete the goal if you created it. Do not complete a pre-existing goal until its own objective is finished.\\n\\n### Delegated-executor instructions\\n\\nEvery delegated prompt must be fully self-contained. Write it for a recipient seeing it as the first message in a new thread, with no access to your transcript or tacit context. Have empathy for that recipient: state every goal, relevant fact, decision, constraint, referent, and requested final action it needs to do the work correctly.\\n\\nBefore delegating, reconstruct the user’s intent from the whole conversation—not only the latest request. Transfer the relevant context, goals, decisions, reasoning, constraints, terminology, changes of mind, rejected approaches, and final direction you have accumulated. Resolve every conversational reference into an explicit description. Never write “the agreed approach,” “as discussed,” “the earlier issue,” or similar shorthand that only makes sense to someone who experienced the original conversation.\\n\\nPrompt length should reflect the amount of real intent that needs to be transferred. A brief request with little context can produce a brief, complete prompt; do not pad it with boilerplate, invented constraints, unsolicited preferences, or generic advice. A long, interactive conversation may require a very long prompt. Do not compress away its twists, revisions, rationale, or tacit intent merely to make the handoff concise. If the user changed direction, make the final direction clear and preserve enough of the reasoning to prevent the recipient from reviving a rejected approach.\\n\\nThe goal is faithful transfer, not brevity or verbosity. Do not invent intent the user never expressed, and do not lose intent the user did express. Before dispatching, read the prompt with empathy for a recipient entering cold: could it understand what the user wants, why the important decisions were made, and what outcome is expected using this prompt alone? If it would need any missing part of your conversation, the prompt is not
